name: Nuratau-Kyzylkum Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Wild sheep, vultures and almond groves where the Nuratau range meets the desert.

tip.title: Take away the spring rain
tip.text: Spring moisture drives the grasses and milkvetches. Set Spring rain to -100% and watch argali and hares, then the wolves, foxes and vultures that depend on them.

sources.title: Uzbekistan government: The Nurata State Reserve

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Bukhara almond
nodes.desc: A wild almond of the Central Asian foothills that grows at roughly 1,000 to 1,800 m. The cinereous vulture nests in Bukhara almond trees in this range, per the Key Biodiversity Areas factsheet.

nodes.name: Wild walnut
nodes.desc: Feral walnut trees grow in the river flood-land forests of the reserve. The nuts are a rich food for animals such as wild boar.

nodes.name: Milkvetches
nodes.desc: Many Oxytropis and Astragalus species are recorded in the Nuratau slopes, some of them local endemics. Their leaves and seeds feed herbivores.

nodes.name: Steppe grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses and sedges cover about 45% of the Nuratau site (grassland), growing fast in the damp spring. They are the main forage on the lower slopes and desert fringe.

nodes.name: Severtsov argali
nodes.desc: A wild mountain sheep. The Nuratau-Kyzylkum reserve is said to hold the only wild population of the Severtsov subspecies. Wikipedia names wolves as the main argali predators.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots for plant foods, nuts and small animals. Listed among the mammals of the Nurata reserve.

nodes.name: Tolai hare
nodes.desc: A hare of Central Asian steppe and desert that eats grasses and herbs. It is common prey for foxes and buzzards.

nodes.name: Yellow ground squirrel
nodes.desc: A large burrowing ground squirrel of Central Asian deserts and steppe. It eats plants and is prey for raptors and foxes.

nodes.name: Chukar
nodes.desc: A rocky-slope game bird that eats seeds, leaves and some insects. Well recorded in the reserve area, and prey for eagles, buzzards and foxes.

nodes.name: Bush-cricket
nodes.desc: A large bush-cricket of dry shrubby ground. It chews leaves and some other insects and feeds lizards and bats.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: An adaptable predator and scavenger. GloBI records it eating many of the birds, hares and lizards of the area.

nodes.name: Booted eagle
nodes.desc: A small eagle that hunts birds, lizards and small mammals. GloBI records link it to chukar, ground squirrels and many small birds.

nodes.name: European glass lizard
nodes.desc: A big legless lizard that eats insects, snails and small vertebrates, including other lizards in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Central Asian racerunner
nodes.desc: A quick small lizard of sandy and stony ground, commonly recorded here. Racerunners generally eat insects.

nodes.name: Eurasian griffon
nodes.desc: A cliff-nesting vulture that feeds on carcasses of large animals. It is listed in the Uzbekistan Red Data Book as a breeder in the range.

nodes.name: Cinereous vulture
nodes.desc: A huge vulture that eats mainly carrion, including carcasses of wild sheep and domestic livestock. Globally threatened, and it breeds in the Nuratau range.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: Listed among the mammals of the Nurata reserve. Wikipedia names wolves as the main predators of argali, especially in hard winters.

nodes.name: Long-legged buzzard
nodes.desc: A raptor of open dry steppe and rocky country. It takes ground squirrels, hares, lizards and chukars, and nests on cliffs.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Long, hot, dry summers drive the desert and foothill plants.

nodes.name: Spring rain & snowmelt
nodes.desc: Moisture comes mainly in the cooler months, so plant growth surges in spring and slows in the hot dry summer.

nodes.name: Rocky shale & desert soil
nodes.desc: The Nurata range is mostly shales, sandstone and limestone, with soils thin and dry in places.

nodes.name: Soil microbes & beetles
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the thin dry soil.
